title: Grade 5 Social Studies — Westward Expansion and Its Consequences
subject: Social Studies
description: Practice with questions on migration, sovereignty, land, removal, perspectives.
creator: Teach Arcade

questions.question: What did the Louisiana Purchase do in 1803?
choices: ended the American Revolution
added a large territory to the United States through an agreement with France
created the first English colony
gave Ohio to France

questions.question: What did Lewis and Clark do after the Louisiana Purchase?
choices: lead the Constitutional Convention
travel and record information on a western expedition
build the first U.S. railroad across the country
write the Declaration of Independence

questions.question: How did Sacagawea help the expedition?
choices: She built a railroad ahead of them.
She wrote the purchase agreement with France.
She interpreted and helped the group communicate and travel.
She was president during the journey.

questions.question: Why is “empty land” inaccurate for much of the area settlers traveled into?
choices: No maps described any western places.
All the land was under ocean water.
People could not live anywhere west of the Mississippi.
Native nations already lived there and governed their communities.

questions.question: What was one reason families used the Oregon Trail?
choices: to return from Europe by ship
to build the first cities near the Atlantic coast
to reach Boston Harbor
to reach new homes and farmland in the West

questions.question: What is one hardship travelers could face on overland trails?
choices: illness and difficult river crossings
a train station in every valley
ocean tides at every campsite
hotel rooms already booked each night

questions.question: What did the Indian Removal Act of 1830 help the federal government do?
choices: make western settlements independent countries
force many Native people from their homelands
create voting rights for all Native people
return every taken acre to Native nations

questions.question: What was the Trail of Tears?
choices: a celebration welcoming people home
a voluntary vacation route
forced removal in which many Cherokee and other Native people suffered and died
the route of the first coast-to-coast railroad

questions.question: Which legal document transferred large areas from Mexico to the United States after the Mexican-American War?
choices: Mayflower Compact
U.S. Bill of Rights
Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo
Treaty of Paris of 1783

questions.question: What drew many newcomers to California in 1849?
choices: the opening of the Erie Canal in California
the discovery of gold
the first flight across the Pacific
the founding of Jamestown

questions.question: What changed when the first transcontinental railroad was completed in 1869?
choices: The United States stopped trading by rail.
Native communities gained back all taken land.
All journeys still took exactly as long as wagon trips.
People and goods could travel across much of the country faster.

questions.question: Which groups labored on the first transcontinental railroad?
choices: only people who had served in the Continental Congress
workers who included many Chinese and Irish immigrants
only state governors
only British veterans of the Revolution

questions.question: What idea was called Manifest Destiny?
choices: a Native nation's general agreement to give up its lands
a treaty requiring the U.S. to stop all expansion
a belief used to justify U.S. expansion across the continent
a plan to move all western towns east

questions.question: Which source best shows the experience of a person on an overland trail?
choices: a diary by a traveler during the journey
a map of today's airports alone
a new calendar with no notes
a modern poster for a train ride in another country

questions.question: Why should a historian compare a settler's letter with a Native nation's account?
choices: Only sources written by settlers can describe the event.
Both sources must give the same reason for moving.
Expansion meant different things to people it affected.
Comparing them makes dates unimportant.

questions.question: What did the Homestead Act offer to eligible applicants who met its conditions?
choices: a way to claim some federal land
the right to remove any border they wanted
a free ship to Europe
a job building any railroad

questions.question: How did expansion change many Native communities' access to land?
choices: Every treaty preserved the same territories.
All Native nations gained the same amount of land.
All communities voluntarily chose identical new homes.
Many were displaced or had access restricted.

questions.question: Which sequence is chronological?
choices: Louisiana Purchase → California Gold Rush → first transcontinental railroad
Louisiana Purchase → first transcontinental railroad → Gold Rush
first transcontinental railroad → Louisiana Purchase → Gold Rush
California Gold Rush → Louisiana Purchase → first transcontinental railroad

questions.question: Which factor most affected where wagon travelers crossed a mountain range?
choices: finding a route through a pass with manageable slopes
avoiding maps of elevation
taking the route with the tallest cliffs
choosing an area with the brightest trail signs

questions.question: Which question best invites study of more than one perspective on expansion?
choices: Why should all maps leave out Native homelands?
Which single letter explains every event?
What one reason did every group share?
How did a new railroad affect settlers, workers, and Native communities differently?
